{"id": "201f98b1-6b31-4c5f-a561-a5a3a35e461a", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "I haven't run anything. Here is the command, with the checks I made first.

**What I checked in us-east-1 (account 012345678901_1)**
- Three running instances have the tag `ssm-skill-test=true`: `i-1234567890abcdef0_4`, `i-1234567890abcdef0_2` and `i-1234567890abcdef0_3`. All three are t3.nano.
- The alarm `ssm-skill-test-cpu` exists. It watches CPUUtilization with a threshold of 99, and it is currently OK.
- `AWS-RestartEC2Instance` is an Automation document. Its parameters are `InstanceId` and `AutomationAssumeRole`.

**Command**

```bash
aws ssm start-automation-execution \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --document-name "AWS-RestartEC2Instance" \
  --target-parameter-name InstanceId \
  --targets "Key=tag:ssm-skill-test,Values=true" \
  --max-concurrency 1 \
  --max-errors 1 \
  --parameters "AutomationAssumeRole=[redacted ARN]<AutomationRoleName>" \
  --alarm-configuration "IgnorePollAlarmFailure=false,Alarms=[{Name=ssm-skill-test-cpu}]"
```

**How it works**
- `--targets` with `--target-parameter-name InstanceId` runs the automation once for each instance carrying the tag. This is rate-controlled mode.
- `--alarm-configuration` makes Systems Manager watch `ssm-skill-test-cpu` while the run is in progress. If the alarm goes to ALARM, the automation stops and no further instances are restarted.
- `IgnorePollAlarmFailure=false` makes the run stop if Systems Manager can't read the alarm state. Set it to `true` if you'd rather it keep going in that case.
- `--max-concurrency 1` restarts one instance at a time. Without it, all three could restart together before the alarm has a chance to stop anything. You can raise it, but then more instances will already be in progress when the alarm fires.
- `--max-errors 1` stops the run after the first failed instance.

**Before you run it**
- Replace `<AutomationRoleName>` with an IAM role that Systems Manager Automation can assume. The role needs permission to stop and start EC2 instances. The alarm configuration also needs `cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms` on the Automation role. Alternatively, leave out `AutomationAssumeRole` to run with your own credentials.
- This command restarts the instances, so each one is briefly unavailable. Instances with instance-store data or no auto-start workloads could be affected.
- A threshold of 99% CPU is hard to reach on a restart, so the alarm probably won't fire during a normal run. I can still add a pre-check or a different threshold if you'd like.

I can run it for you if you give me the role ARN. Each action needs your approval before it executes.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
